claims.text: A machine-learning model trained on HEA data can accurately identify high-entropy alloys with low phonon thermal conductivity.
The model uses atomic mass variance, lattice distortion, and electronic structure as predictive features.
The machine-learning approach will improve predictive accuracy by at least 20% relative to traditional physics-based models.
Atomic mass variance in HEAs scatters phonons.
Lattice distortion in HEAs scatters phonons.
Phonon scattering caused by atomic mass variance and lattice distortion reduces thermal conductivity.
A machine-learning model can capture complex, nonlinear relationships between the selected material features and phonon thermal conductivity.
Traditional physics-based models of phonon thermal conductivity rely on simplified assumptions.
Capturing nonlinear feature–conductivity relationships enables more accurate predictions than traditional physics-based models.
The approach is applicable to HEAs whose compositions and structural configurations are similar to those represented in the training data.
The approach may not generalize to HEAs with substantially different compositions or processing histories.
Model performance may degrade if the training dataset is not sufficiently large and diverse to represent the relevant HEA feature space.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% predictive-accuracy improvement over traditional physics-based models on a separate HEA validation set would falsify the hypothesis.
